div.p: What the confidante who made [her] agree to going away together said to HER.

lg.l: oḷiyac ceṉmār celka veṉṟunā
maḻipaṭa ruḻakku mavala neñcat
tevva mikantucē ṇakala vaiyeyiṟ
ṟūṇacaip piṇavi ṉuṟupaci kaḷaiiya
kāṭutēr maṭappiṇai yalaṟak kalaiyi
ṉōṭukuṟaṅ kaṟutta cennā yēṟṟai
veyilpulan tiḷaikkum vemmaip payilviri
yirumpuli vēṅkai karuṅkō laṉṉa
kalleṭut teṟinta palkiḻi yuṭukkai
yulaṟukuṭai vampala ruyarmara mēṟi
yēṟuvēṭ ṭeḻunta viṉantī reruvai
yāṭucevi nōkku mattam paṇaittōṭ
kuvaḷai yuṇka ṇivaḷu nammoṭu
varumeṉ ṟaṉarē kātalar
vārāy tōḻi muyaṅkukam palavē.
So that trouble goes far beyond
the suffering heart that bears desolate affliction,
thinking “let us set out to go in secret,
[your] lover said: “she too, with bamboo shoulders
[and] waterlily kajal eyes will come with us,”
on the road, where travellers with worn-out umbrellas,
[their] garments [made] of many pieces of cloth on which stones were lifted [and] thrown,
like the black leaf-stems of the kino tree , a big/black tiger, densely expanding,
climb on high trees [and] look at the moving ears
of the group-leaving kite that has risen to hunt the bull,
[come with us] through the heat when, vexed with the sunlight,
the male of the red dog becomes lean that had taken off the running thigh
of the stag, so that [its] youthful doe cries out, searching the wilderness,
in order to remove the hunger felt by the sharp-toothed bitch that yearns for food.
Come, friend, we will embrace many [times].
on the road, where the group-leaving kite that has risen to hunt the bull
climbs a high tree [and] with moving ears looks at
the travellers with worn-out umbrellas who lift [and] throw stones [at it],
